Key.English: Class Picker
Collect building, vehicle and unit classnames by looking at them. Sync it to the placement modules it is picking for. Editor preview only.

SYNC THIS MODULE TO THE PLACEMENT MODULES IT IS PICKING FOR. The sync lines are what tell it which modules to fill in, and what it offers you in game follows them: sync it to military placement and it offers to fill military garrisons, and leaves civilian ones out. Sync it to as many as you like. Without any sync it still works, but nothing can be written back on its own, and the list has to be applied by hand to a module you select.
LEAVE IT IN THE MISSION WHEN YOU ARE DONE. It works only when previewing from the editor, and hosted and dedicated sessions ignore it entirely, so a released mission is unaffected and players are never given the picker keys. Keeping it placed means its settings and its sync lines are still there the next time you want to change what gets garrisoned, instead of having to wire it all up again.
Collect classnames for settings that ask for them, by looking at things instead of typing them. Every object of the chosen kind near you is labelled with its class. Home collects the one under the crosshair. On a building, End also collects the numbered position under the crosshair, so a garrison list can be built by looking at the windows you want filled. Come back to the editor and what you picked goes into the modules this one is synced to.
Collect:
What to label and collect. Buildings for garrison positions and strategic house lists, Vehicles and Units for the blacklists. Aiming at a soldier also picks up the group he was spawned from.
Range:

How far around YOU to look, in metres. Nothing further away than this is labelled, however you are standing. Larger ranges label more at once and cost more to draw in a dense town, so 75 is a good starting point and walking to the next street is cheaper than raising it. This is not what decides which buildings count: when the picker is synced to placement modules, only buildings inside those modules' areas are labelled, however close to you anything else is.
Show position numbers:
Number the standing positions inside the building under the crosshair, so a position can be chosen by looking at it. Turn off when collecting classnames only.
Start on preview:

Whether labelling begins the moment the preview starts. No by default, so nothing is drawn until you ask for it from the ALiVE menu, which keeps the labels out of the way when you are previewing for some other reason. Set to Yes to have it start on its own.
On returning to the editor:

What to do with what you picked when the preview ends. Apply to synced modules writes it straight into the placement modules this picker is synced to, which is usually what you want. Remind me says what was collected and leaves it to you. Either way you can always apply it by hand from the right click menu, and Ctrl+Z takes it back.
Classname size:
Height of the classname labels. Raise it if they are hard to read against a bright sky.
Position number size:
Height of the position numbers. Larger than the classnames by default, since these are aimed at rather than only read.
Label font:
Font the labels are drawn in. PuristaBold reads well against both sky and ground. Any font from CfgFontFamilies works.
Start picking %1
Label everything of the chosen kind nearby
Stop picking
Remove the labels. What has been collected is kept, so it can still be copied.
Take what I am looking at
Remove what I am looking at
Remove position %1
Same as pressing Home. Takes what you are looking at, or gives it back if it is already held.
Take the position I am looking at
Same as pressing End. Takes the numbered position you are looking at, or gives it back if it is already held. The order positions are taken in is the order they get filled in.
Take every position in this building
Remove every position in this building

Take all the numbered positions in the building you are looking at, or give them all back if you already hold every one. Positions already taken keep the order you gave them and the rest are added after.
Copy for a setting (%1) >
Put what you have collected on the clipboard, in the form the setting you name wants it in
Copy for
Military Placement garrisons
Military Placement garrisons (%1 synced)
Civilian Placement garrisons (%1 synced)
Preferred Garrison Buildings on a military placement module. Back in the editor, select the module and apply it from the right click menu.
Civilian Placement garrisons
Preferred Garrison Buildings on a civilian placement module. Back in the editor, select the module and apply it from the right click menu.
Keep garrisons out of this building
Let garrisons use this building again

Adds the building you are looking at to the garrison blacklist, or takes it off again if it is already on. Same as pressing Delete. The blacklist is kept apart from the buildings you take with Home, so excluding something never disturbs the positions you picked.
Garrison building blacklist (%1)
Garrison building blacklist

Buildings no garrison should ever put men in. Look at a building and press Delete to collect it, then choose this to copy the list. Delete keeps its own list, separate from the buildings collected with Home, so excluding something never disturbs the positions you picked. Applying it in the editor puts the classes into every placement module's Garrison Building Blacklist. Positions are not needed here, so any you collected are ignored.
Vehicle blacklist
ALiVE_PLACEMENT_CUSTOM_VEHICLEBLACKLIST, pasted into the mission's init.sqf
Unit blacklist
ALiVE_PLACEMENT_CUSTOM_UNITBLACKLIST, pasted into the mission's init.sqf
Group blacklist
ALiVE_PLACEMENT_CUSTOM_GROUPBLACKLIST, pasted into the mission's init.sqf. Uses the groups picked up from soldiers.
Copy for garrison positions (%1)
Class=1,2,3;Class2=0,4 ready to paste into Preferred Garrison Buildings. Buildings with no positions taken are left out.
Copy as a plain list
Class1,Class2 ready to paste into a text field in the editor
Copy as an array
["Class1","Class2"] ready to paste into a setting in init.sqf
Copy the groups
The group classes picked up from soldiers, ready for a group blacklist
Clear everything collected
Empty the list and start again
